title: Content-Security-Policy font-src allows a wildcard source
description: The Content-Security-Policy font-src directive allows a bare wildcard source: the token `*` or a scheme wildcard such as `https://*` appears inside that directive's source list. The policy therefore permits the browser to load the affected resource type from any origin, which is the opposite of what a restrictive policy is meant to express. Fonts can be loaded from any origin, so a page can render attacker-chosen faces and leak short text through which glyphs the browser requests.
remediation: Replace the wildcard in font-src with the explicit origins that must be reachable, and use 'none' or 'self' where no third-party origin is needed. If the wildcard was added to unblock a single vendor, name that vendor's origin instead so the policy keeps recording intent.
limitation: One header value and one directive. The rule judges font-src only when it is written in the policy; when the directive is absent, the default-src or child-src fallback decides the behaviour and other rules report that case. Values are matched lexically, so an origin wildcard such as *.example.com is not treated as a bare wildcard.
